stories.title: The group chat that bonds Black NBA coaches off the court
stories.summary: On the court, they're rivals. Off the court, they've found support among the only men who truly understand what they're going through: each other.
stories.detailText: DETROIT PISTONS COACH J.B. Bickerstaff and then- Orlando Magic coach Jamahl Mosley broke the ice after nearly two weeks of silence: a simple bro hug at midcourt before their teams played Game 7 of last season's first-round series. More than a series was on the line -- jobs have been decided in these situations, and that series was no different. Regardless, the two consider themselves brothers. "We didn't make eye contact during the series," Bickerstaff said. "I knew the outcome of that series -- we played two years before when I was in Cleveland -- if I would've lost to Jamahl, I would've been fired. I knew if Jamahl didn't beat us [last season], he was going to be fired. "Coaching those games was extremely emotional, and them both coming down to Game 7s adds more weight to those moments. I know the impact that it has on you, your wife in that moment. His kids call me Uncle." Several coaches closely watched the matchup. They are part of an 11-member group chat featuring Black NBA head coaches and assistants who have been friends for years. "For us, it was fun," Indiana Pacers associate head coach Lloyd Pierce said. "It was Game 7. You don't have to put that face on anymore for your players. They knew. This is results oriented. Someone's going home, someone ain't. But it's all love. They had to be professionals, but it was a beautiful moment for our group." Pierce and Washington Wizards assistant David Vanterpool couldn't wait to show the video of the two close friends' hug before the game at their annual "wine and conversation" event that takes place during summer league. It exemplified the community they have striven to create: two fierce competitors in their natural element who, behind the scenes, are friends in any other group chat, commiserating over shared experiences and struggles, talking about issues of the world in a space where they knew it would stay without judgment. And doing so with the only men who can identify with what they are going through: each other. There are nine Black head coaches in the NBA -- three fewer than last season with Jason Kidd, Chauncey Billups and Doc Rivers no longer with their franchises. When Kidd and Boston 's Joe Mazzulla met in the 2024 NBA Finals, it was the first time two Black coaches faced each other in the Finals since 1975, when Al Attles' Golden State Warriors swept K.C. Jones' Washington Bullets. It's been cyclical, but the NBA had recently reached a high mark for Black coaches. There were 15 in 2022-23 and 14 the following season. In the 2019-20 season, that number was just seven. This collective, which as a group chat has expanded into other events, has become an outlet to discuss opportunities that have come and ones that haven't. But it has also expanded into a network of support and connections that extends far beyond the court. The connections are so intertwined -- coaches who have served under one another and been introduced through members of the group chat -- it's almost too many to name. "It's the most important thing we have in this business," Bickerstaff said. "Like nothing gets done in the NBA without connections and community. So like us being able to build a community has changed the outlook and the window of opportunity for people." Hours after Bickerstaff and Mosley embraced ahead of their Game 7 meeting, the top-seeded Pistons beat the eighth-seeded Magic, completing a comeback from being down 3-1 in the series. Shortly after, Bickerstaff's thoughts drifted to Mosley and his future. "You're extremely excited about what's next for you, and you have to prepare for that," Bickerstaff said. "But you're also walking around with the weight of what happens to someone you care about." Mosley was fired 24 hours later. Two weeks later, the New Orleans Pelicans hired him . NO ONE CAN REMEMBER when the group chat started, who started it or even the original coaches who were in it -- some were added after the initial iteration. What they all agreed on was how quickly it became a place for coaches at different stages of their lives and careers to vent, seek advice, talk about the world and do so freely. New York Knicks coach Mike Brown is the oldest at 56. Charlotte Hornets assistant coach John Bryant (not to be confused with Cleveland Cavaliers assistant coach Johnnie Bryant, who's also part of the group chat) is the youngest, not yet 40. It also includes Bickerstaff, Mosley, Pierce, Vanterpool, former Memphis Grizzlies and Knicks coach David Fizdale, Philadelphia 76ers assistant Phil Handy, former Los Angeles Lakers coach and current Milwaukee Bucks assistant Darvin Ham and Wizards assistant J.J. Outlaw. Like any group chat, there are jokes -- and nobody is off-limits. Brown's viral demand and demonstration, showing Sacramento Kings players what it's like to sprint back on defense (" turn the f---ing jets on !") made the rounds. "We gave Mike s--- about that for two hours," Pierce said of Brown's moment in Sacramento. Fizdale's " take that for data " slam during the 2017 NBA playoffs when he was coaching the Grizzlies against the San Antonio Spurs was another moment, both for its seriousness and its virality. "If you do something and somebody finds a clip and puts it out there, make no mistake," Pierce said. "Fiz went viral and next thing you know someone makes a light skin joke and it's not about the clip anymore. It's about the jokes now. Classic group chat stuff." The friendships started with hoops and Hall of Famer Tim Grgurich's annual basketball camp in Las Vegas. Those four-day summer sessions were a place for the league to convene and for upward of 50 young players and 30 coaches to sharpen their tools. Younger coaches worked one-on-one with current players and also met with older coaches to network. After a long day of work, the coaches would hang out late into the night. "We were still the first ones in the gym the next morning," Pierce said. "We were the guys that were running Grug camp, and coaches and front offices were taking notice of that. Our energy, our ability to connect with players at a high level on the court." While camps such as Grgurich's often serve as laboratories for coaches to hone new strategies, the group chat doesn't talk about basketball philosophy as much. "We never really crossed that line. It's not a venting spot [about our teams]," Pierce said. "Somebody might send an awareness text, 'Anybody see this?' And we'll break off from there." Pierce, Bickerstaff and Ham are the most vocal about granular basketball issues, with Bickerstaff being head of the NBA Coaches Association. When Vanterpool, then an associate head coach in Minnesota, was passed over for then-Raptors assistant Chris Finch after Ryan Saunders was fired in February 2021, Pierce was one of the main voices who spoke out in support of Vanterpool. The group became closer in 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic converged with a nationwide social justice uprising. Brown led a weekly Zoom call for Black coaches. The group organized Peloton rides to bond together. Pierce and Bickerstaff became vocal after George Floyd's death, coming up with the Coaches for Racial Justice initiative. "There's a security. Say whatever the hell you want to say," Pierce said. "Johnny Bryant, John Bryant and J.J. Outlaw are the young pups. They've usually sat in the background, so to speak, because they know if, you know, they pop off, we all kind of gang up on them like big brothers." BICKERSTAFF JOINED FIZDALE as an assistant on the Grizzlies when Bickerstaff's run as the Houston Rockets ' interim head coach ended after the 2015-16 season. Outlaw, the only one in the group chat with a heavy football background -- he played wide receiver at Villanova before turning back to basketball -- was also on the staff. He had previously served as a video coordinator for Brown with the Lakers. "My unique contribution to the group, having a different perspective," Outlaw said. "My path to get into coaching was different. That group gave me a lot of confidence." Outlaw remembers being at Grgurich's camp and Pierce approaching him for one of their first conversations. "He said, 'Take me through your defensive philosophies,' which is basically, 'Take me through Mike Brown's defensive philosophy,'" Outlaw said. "I didn't have one of my own at that time." Outlaw went through it, talking about shrinking the floor, playing with activity, not giving up the middle of the floor. Pierce nodded but didn't say much until Outlaw finished. "He said, 'I worked for Mike in Cleveland. I knew the answer. I wanted to make sure you knew the answer.' That was big for me. Lloyd cares about people, and J.B., too," Outlaw said. There have been times when support was needed even beyond the job. During the 2023 first-round series between the Cavaliers and Knicks, Outlaw's wife was close to giving birth, and his mother was battling ovarian cancer. His son was born on a Sunday and brought home on a Wednesday. The next day, doctors gave him some sobering news: There was nothing more they could do for his mother. "Who do you share that information with? You don't want the league to know; you want your private life to be that," Outlaw said. For Bickerstaff, Outlaw was his godbrother and Outlaw's mother was his "Aunt Linda." "That's my second mom. I know what he's going through, what his dad is going through," Bickerstaff said. "It's the greatest system of support in our position that you can have. A group of people who understand exactly what you're going through from a professional standpoint and how heavy that can be and also support you in your personal life as well." Pierce's wife and Ham's wife had been diagnosed with breast cancer, thus adding a new depth to their conversations. They were able to trade notes and lean on each other in what can often feel like a helpless situation. "I could see the fear," Ham said of his wife, who was initially diagnosed in 2021 before the Bucks won the NBA title. "[In August], we got a clean bill of health." BROWN STOOD IN front of the crowd at the annual wine and conversation event in Las Vegas in 2025, showing more emotion on this night than when he led the Knicks to an NBA title less than a year later. The event, a quiet highlight of summer league, is the culmination of what was born at Grgurich's camp. The coaches were able to go from being a small group hanging out in Vegas having dinner at the Wynn one year, to each bringing another coach with them the next year to get them around like-minded folks, to gathering enough momentum in a few years to host the sponsored event. Coaches and front office execs gather for a couple of hours for a panel discussion and to celebrate an honoree -- a longtime head coach receiving his flowers for his dedication to the game. Usually eloquent, Brown could barely get his words out, trying to find the right ones to describe his relationship with Bernie Bickerstaff, whom the coaches were honoring with a lifetime achievement award that night. The elder Bickerstaff hired Brown as a video coordinator for the Denver Nuggets after Brown finished his playing career at San Diego in 1992. Ironically, one of his tasks was keeping an eye on J.B. Bickerstaff, nine years his junior. Little did anyone know the roots of this group would begin with those two men: Brown and Bickerstaff. "I don't want to make this about my dad, but it's kind of a gap-bridger," Bickerstaff said. J.J. Outlaw's dad, John, grew up with Bernie Bickerstaff. J.B., whose full name is John-Blair, was named after John Outlaw. When Brown was hired by the elder Bickerstaff, he would help with J.J., filming some of his football games. So when Outlaw climbed back into basketball, Brown called in need of a video coordinator. "It was New Year's Eve and the season started on Christmas [in 2011] and asked me did I want the job," Outlaw said. "I asked him when did he need me, and he said, 'yesterday.'" Two days later, Outlaw began his coaching journey on a staff with Ham, who he knew back when Ham was playing for Bernie Bickerstaff's Nuggets in the late '90s. "Bernie changed the whole trajectory of my family's life, man," Outlaw said. "I'm an only child, so I have a brother in J.B. who I grew up with, who's five years older, who you know is looking out for me and mentoring me and getting on my ass and cussing me out every other day." His story isn't dissimilar to many of the coaches in the group. Whether they knew it or not when they first connected, a community was being built. When Fizdale received his first head coaching opportunity in Memphis in 2016, it was proof that the struggles coaches experienced -- almost all of them without NBA playing experience -- had a finish line. "There's a real pathway for all of us," Pierce said. "I remember sending a message saying, 'What you've done is create and represented all of us, and you've given all of us an opportunity to now be looked at as head coaches.' It was what we needed to stay the course and keep doing what we were doing. The fear was, we were going to have to conform." Pierce got his chance years later, coaching the Atlanta Hawks from 2018 to 2021, then landed on Rick Carlisle's staff in Indiana the next year, a critical element of its franchise turnaround. The younger Bickerstaff began cementing himself in Cleveland, where he finally landed a head coaching opportunity in 2019 . He went to Detroit in 2024 and led it to a 60-win record last season. "The strength of our community is the talent," Bickerstaff said. "I get let go in Cleveland, J.J. is good enough to get a job somewhere else. Lloyd gets let go and immediately has options. There's a talent level to the group where you know we don't feel like we're just carrying around dead weight." Those long nights of work have turned into talks about fatherhood and parenting and real estate and politics, and they gathered again for recent weddings and vacations over the summer. It's also why they have a special appreciation for the man who finally joined the fraternity of champions this past June in Brown -- who was given a standing ovation at this year's wine and conversation weeks after leading New York to its first title in 53 years. "There's a common connection with Mike -- it's why we honor him so much," Pierce said. "Seeing Mike, because of his experiences in the past. Being let go in Sacramento was a joke, being let go in L.A. was a joke. Knowing how good he is, for everyone to see he's all that we've talked about and now he's got a championship, so now you know it too, it's refreshing." And the group chat let him know it.

stories.title: Veteran center Mason Plumlee signing with Kings
stories.summary: Mason Plumlee, who is entering his 14th NBA season, is signing a deal with Sacramento, his representatives told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detailText: Free agent center Mason Plumlee is signing a deal with the Sacramento Kings , his representatives, Mark Bartelstein and Andy Shiffman of Priority Sports, told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday. Plumlee is entering his 14th NBA season. He played last season for the Charlotte Hornets and San Antonio Spurs , appearing in 20 games with three starts. He averaged 1.6 points and 2.7 rebounds in 8.6 minutes. His last consistent action came in 2024-25 with the Phoenix Suns , where he played in 74 games and averaged 4.5 points and 6.1 rebounds. The Kings are off to a 1-10 start that had them tied for last place in the league entering Wednesday's games. They had an open roster spot after Sunday's trade of second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder for two second-round picks.

stories.summary: The Celtics will start Baylor Scheierman and two centers — Neemias Queta and Luka Garza — when they face off against the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday.
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CA - JANUARY 3: Luka Garza #52 and Neemias Queta #88 of the Boston Celtics high five during the game against the LA Clippers on January 3, 2026 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images TORONTO — The Celtics will start Derrick White, Baylor Scheierman, Jayson Tatum, Neemias Queta, and Luka Garza on Wednesday night when they face the Toronto Raptors. It will be Garza’s first start of the season and Scheierman’s second. Paul George, fresh off a 36-point outing against the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, is out with illness. Celtics starters tonight: Derrick White Baylor Scheierman Jayson Tatum Neemias Queta Luka Garza — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) November 11, 2026 The Celtics will start with a double-big lineup for the first time this season. Garza is averaging 6.5 points and 3.5 rebounds in 12.5 minutes per game, while shooting a team-best 52% from three. Queta has started the last six games since coming off the bench to begin the year. Garza, for one, is happy to get the chance to play double-big. “It just gives me another avenue to get on the floor, especially with the bigs that we have and the depth that we have,” Garza said last week of the double-big lineup. “So for me, it’s something I’m going to commit to and buy into trying to be the most effective at that position.” Scheierman, meanwhile, is averaging 5.8 points and 3.7 rebounds in 20 minutes per game, and has also been among the team’s most reliable three-point shooters, hitting 45.2% of his attempts from beyond the arc. For the Raptors, RJ Barrett, Collin Murray-Boyles, Jakob Poeltl, Immanuel Quickley, and Ja’Kobe Walter will start. The Raptors are without both Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes. Joe Mazzulla and the Celtics have regularly shifted starting lineups this season On Sunday against the Milwaukee Bucks, Mike Conley got his first start of the season, which he later revealed to CelticsBlog was a decision made by Jayson Tatum and Derrick White. On Sunday morning, Mazzulla walked into the Celtics’ team meeting and asked the room who should start; Jordan Walsh started in 6 of the Celtics’ first 9 games, while Hugo Gonzalez got the chance in three of them. “He was like, ‘So who’s starting?’” Conley recalled. “He left it up to his players. And JT is like, ‘Mike, me…,’ and gave the starting lineup. I’m like, it’s real.” In addition to Wednesday’s starters, Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez, Jordan Walsh, Mitchell Robinson, and Conley have all gotten the opportunity to start this season. Celtics-Raptors tips off at 7pm ET.

stories.title: Curry confronts critics over comments about wife Ayesha
stories.summary: Warriors star Stephen Curry took to social media Wednesday to address criticisms of wife Ayesha's acting role in "Second Chance Holiday."
stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry took to social media Wednesday to address criticisms made of the acting role his wife, Ayesha, has in "Second Chance Holiday." Former NBA players Nick Young -- who won a ring with Steph in 2017-18 -- and Gilbert Arenas reacted to the topic of Ayesha's kissing scene on the "We Said What We Said" podcast Saturday. "The only blemish in the family is the wife in the sense because she doesn't act like the other superstars' wives. [Michael] Jordan's wife, Cookie [Johnson], that's Magic's [Johnson's] wife, Savannah [James], right, where we don't want to hear you," Arenas said on the podcast. "She hasn't been the American wife that the public knows." Arenas went further, saying they "want" Ayesha's kissing scene to be a problem because "Steph is so innocent." "I've been hearing a lot of noise and usually the noise doesn't bother me, doesn't bother Ayesha but, this one in particular when you try to step on the accomplishments of my wife and you know, obviously, leading podcast tapings and topics, giving opinions on somebody else's wife," Steph said, "Nick, Gil, Emmanuel [Acho] and anybody else who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you really don't know about. "Something that kind of speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do, even the ignorance behind how acting works, obviously I tried to laugh this off but something needs to be said." Ayesha comes from an acting background that includes appearances in several films, such as "Irish Wish" and "Joy to the World," and the TV show "Hannah Montana" in her early career. "Anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, I'd kindly suggest you just give the happy hands, the congratulations and maybe the apology as loud as you lead your shows with this topic," Steph said. "Appreciate the free pub." Shortly after Steph addressed Arenas and Young's comments on social media, the duo issued an apology on "Gil's Arena." "I'm sorry Steph. You my dog, I love you. If I say anything, I apologize like a man," Young said. "I'm sorry if he's offended. I didn't mean it like that. I was just saying he's such a perfect dude," Arenas said. "Second Chance Holiday" premiered on the Roku channel Thursday.

stories.title: Donovan Mitchell details Coco Jones wedding, music passion on 'The Tonight Show'
stories.summary: The Cavs guard revealed wedding details and a new hobby in his appearance on "The Tonight Show."
stories.detailText: It's no coincidence Donovan Mitchell is married to R&B singer-songwriter Coco Jones. They share the language they both love: music. On Tuesday night, the Cleveland Cavaliers star guard appeared as a guest on "The Tonight Show" with Jimmy Fallon, where he spoke about being married to the Grammy Award-winning artist. The couple tied the knot back in August. Mitchell, who proposed to the singer in July 2025, says he "planned" the music for the wedding and joked about his idea of planning the ceremony before going into detail about how their big day was set up. "We had two tents. She wanted a real intimate ceremony, and I was like 'I'm inviting my third grade teacher; I'm inviting everybody,'" Mitchell said. In one tent, Mitchell says there were around 40 people for an intimate ceremony. Once attendees walked out to the left, he describes, there was a bigger tent dedicated to the wedding reception. "That was my part of the wedding," Mitchell jokes. What began as a conversation between Mitchell and Fallon quickly transitioned into the Cavs guard's love for music. And from what the couple danced to at their wedding -- Musiq Soulchild's "Love" -- he's got immaculate music taste. Mitchell then shared a bit about his musical background, which consisted of him playing the drums before he ever set foot on an NBA court. He said he started playing drums in the fourth grade, with his inspiration stemming from his mom having pots and pans and him banging on the dishes to produce sound. "I told [Questlove] I'm coming for your job soon," Mitchell said, prompting the six-time Grammy Award winner -- who anchors Fallon's house band, The Roots -- to hold up his drumsticks in a joking fashion. Mitchell revealed that he recently got into DJing since Jones gave him a DJ controller board. He recalled going back to his alma mater, Louisville, and performing a two-hour set off the top. "Everybody loved it," Mitchell said. The guard is averaging 22.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 5.5 assists in the 2026-27 regular season, but in his downtime, music could be a calming point for the seven-time All-Star.

stories.title: Nets throw-back, Barclays Center voted among NBA’s best
stories.summary: We’re No. 2 and No. 4!
stories.detailText: Well, at least the Nets new throw-back jerseys don’t suck. In USA Today’s Readers’ Choice survey of fan takes on things not related to on-court wins and losses (thank goodness) the Brooklyn Nets scored in two big categories: their ABA-themed throw back jerseys and arena experience. Both finished in top five. The jerseys ranked No. 2 in the survey , behind only the Minnesota Timberwolves (really?), with USA Today writing: It’s been a minute, but true ball knowers will remember Darryl Dawkins and Buck Williams running the floor for the Nets in the 1980’s. In 2026, it almost feels like Jackie Moon should be wearing this jersey, and we love it. In the arena experience category, Barclays Center ranked No. 4 behind Paycomm Center in OKC, Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, and Delta Center in Salt Lake City. Time flies. It felt like just yesterday when Barclays Center opened, and now it is in its 14th year. The venue offers some of the best sightlines for basketball, complementing its amenities. It is known for its culinary offerings. Foodies will love spending a game there—something for everyone, with plenty of support for fans and families. Despite the praise for the Barclays menu, the arena didn’t make the list for best food. The Nets arena is midway in a five-year, $150 million upgrade. Meanwhile, over at the Ringer, which does have a good story on the Nets , Bill Simmons ranks the Nets among the “most screwed teams” in the NBA. Oh well, there’s always the jerseys.

stories.title: Embiid, LeBron questionable for Sixers-Raptors
stories.summary: The Sixers could be without both LeBron James and Joel Embiid when they take on the Toronto Raptors.

(Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Sixers released their injury report for their upcoming battle against the Toronto Raptors, and Joel Embiid and LeBron James are both listed as questionable. Embiid is once again listed with plantar fasciitis management in his right foot and LeBron with the lower back management that he’s also been listed with all season. The good news is there doesn’t seem to be any additional designation for Embiid after he turned his left ankle in an awkward moment in their loss to the Celtics. Embiid didn’t say much about it after the game other than he just turned it and is feeling good. The aforementioned play is below, please excuse the caption. Joel Embiid was on the ground in pain and VJ Edgecombe just YAMMED it over him 😭 (via NBC) pic.twitter.com/2C957jWnii — TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 11, 2026 With that being said, Embiid has struggled so far this season, and has especially looked rough in games since the plantar fasciitis popped up on the injury report about a week and a half ago. In his last three games, two of which were losses, he’s averaged 13.3 points per game and has shot 9-of-37 from the field. He’s also looked noticeably worse on defense in that time period as well. It wouldn’t be the worst thing in the world to get Embiid off of his feet for a couple days, but it’s tough to do so when the team has lost two of it’s last three and has played it’s worst basketball since the start of the season. It only gets trickier if LeBron also isn’t able to play against Toronto. This is the first game LeBron has appeared on the injury report so far this season that is not a back-to-back. After the Sixers play the Raptors, they’re not in action until Nov. 15 when they host Indiana. The Sixers could be very shorthanded in the frontcourt against the Raptors as Adem Bona will miss his fourth straight game with a cervical spine sprain, the team has yet to provide a further update on him. Dominick Barlow remains out, still yet to make his season debut with what is now listed as a lower back stress reaction. On the other hand, Toronto will be playing Philadelphia on the second night of a back-to-back. They don’t have to submit their injury report quite yet, but Scottie Barnes has missed their last three games with a groin strain. The team also announced that Kawhi Leonard, who’s been out since the second game of the season, will miss at least another week, so the Sixers definitely won’t see him. stories.title: Payton Pritchard posted an underrated performance to power Boston over Philly
stories.summary: Pritchard was a team-high +26 for the game, and provided timely buckets throughout
stories.detailText: Nov 10, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Boston Celtics guard Payton Pritchard (11) reacts after a score against the Philadelphia 76ers during the fourth quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The game everyone in the basketball world had circled on their calendars has come and gone. Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics took on Jaylen Brown and the Philadelphia 76ers for the first time on Tuesday night, a matchup with some extra drama tacked on to the already existing Boston-Philly rivalry. The headlines were dominated by the relationship between Jayson and Jaylen, before and after the game. Though a much smaller narrative, this was also Paul George’s return to Philadelphia for the first time since being traded. Ultimately, PG stole the show, scoring a game-high 36 points, knocking down 6 threes, and shooting 14-22 (63.6%) from the floor to lead Boston to a resounding victory, 123-101. George dominated the game, but it was a team victory, and maybe one of the most unspoken heroes of the game is Payton Pritchard. Despite the final score, this matchup had some ups and downs. Boston took a 16-point lead in the second quarter, which Philly got down to 11 before halftime. They came out with a strong push in the third quarter too, tying the game at 76 with four minutes left in the period. They were never able to break the seal, though, thanks in big part to Payton. Philly was on a 7-0 run before taking a timeout to give Dean Wade a breather after he took a stinger fighting through a screen. Coming out of the break, Pritch was being guarded by VJ Edgecombe. Boston, wanting to give him a more advantageous matchup, had Tatum and Mitchell Robinson set a couple screens for him near the logo, putting Payton in position to attack Joel Embiid coming downhill. With Embiid backing up to stop the drive, Pritchard pulled up and knocked down a wide-open three, nothing but nylon. Tyrese Maxey responded with a deep three of his own on the other end, tying the game back up at 79 apiece. The Philly crowd was rising to the moment, fueling the push from the Sixers, and the Celtics wanted to stem it. They ran the same action which freed Pritchard up the first time, this time with Maxey taking the defensive assignment. Tatum was able to screen well enough to give Payton some breathing room, and despite a late closeout from Maxey, Payton used some nice touch and a little bit of Celtic luck to nail another three, a shot that went off the back rim, bounced off the top of the backboard, and found its way through the net, taking all the air out of the moment for the Philly faithful. "OFF THE HEEL, OFF THE TOP… SHOOTER'S TOUCH!" Payton Pritchard (15 PTS, 3 3PM) gets the WILD three to fall 👌 pic.twitter.com/kiwBuDD81f — NBA (@NBA) November 11, 2026 Those two plays from Pritchard started off what was a 29-to-6 run over the next 7.5 minutes. Within that run, Boston hit nine straight threes, four of which Payton contributed himself, and one which he assisted. That run allowed the Celtics to coast for the rest of the game, Nick Nurse making the decision to pull his starters with 5:35 left in the fourth. Payton was responsible for 18 points, 5 assists, 6 rebounds, and a steal, all without committing a single turnover. He had a steady hand throughout, shooting 7-15 (46.7%) from the floor and 4-8 (50%) from three. Pritchard also ended the night as a game-high +26. There’s no question that the new buddy duo of PG and J were the stars of the show, but Boston doesn’t get the win without Payton’s contributions. He rose to the moment, and played off of the Celtics stars, giving the game exactly what it needed, when it needed it. Boston will continue to rely on Pritchard to be a vital part of their offense as they look to build upon the victory and maintain their new spot atop the Eastern Conference.

stories.title: Kirk Cousins plans to talk to Jakobe Thomas about No. 8
stories.summary: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday.
stories.detailText: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday. He still doesn't officially have a number. Has he spoken to rookie safety Jakobe Thomas, who currently wears No. 8? "I need to circle back with him," Cousins told reporters. "Haven't gotten there. So we'll have a conversation and I think Mike Parsons will help us, too, in the equipment room. But, yeah, I've got to talk to Jakobe for sure." When the issue came up again later, Cousins laughed — while also making his intentions clear: "I'm confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy and mature conversation and figure this out." It's hard to imagine Thomas standing in Cousins's way. There are too many Vikings fans who still have No. 8 jerseys that will become moot if Cousins isn't wearing it. However it goes, it would be a shock if Cousins isn't wearing No. 8 on Sunday at Lambeau Field.

stories.title: Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant meet again as Warriors head to Houston
stories.summary: Steph and KD square off for the 41st time, with the Warriors chasing nine straight and Durant looking to make it 8–3.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 2: Yaxel Lendeborg #1 and Brandin Podziemski #2 of the Golden State Warriors high five during the game against the Phoenix Suns on November 2, 2026 at Chase Center in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Back in the day, guys weren’t supposed to be this good this late. Kareem was the exception everybody pointed to for decades, still putting up 23.4 a night and making All-NBA at 38. LeBron is the recent exception. Everybody else got the farewell tour, the rocking chair at the end of the bench, and the jersey ceremony. If you’ve ever iced a rec-league knee after a Tuesday night run, take a good long look at Steph Curry and Kevin Durant tonight. While most 38-year olds are having to take a day off of work to go see their medical provider for their aching spines, these two are doing something most 25 year old hoopers can’t do. As of Nov. 9, of the 38 players in the league averaging at least 20 points, only two were older than 35, and they’ll be on the same floor in Houston. That’s love of the game, plus years of cold tubs, film sessions, and a burning desire to dominate. Golden State Warriors at Houston Rockets When: November 11th, 2026 | 6:30 PM PT TV: ESPN Radio: 95.7 The Game ANOTHER CHAPTER of Steph vs. KD 🔥 Steph Curry and Kevin Durant battle for the 41st time in their careers as the red-hot 8-3 Warriors seek their 9th straight win against the 8-3 Rockets! 9:30pm/et • ESPN pic.twitter.com/If8FjDEQQj — NBA (@NBA) November 11, 2026 STEPH/KD AS TEAMMATES: 🔥 3 seasons 🔥 2 championships 🔥 164-46 record 🔥 Curry: 26.0 PPG, 5.1 RPG, 5.9 APG 🔥 Durant: 26.0 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 5.2 APG STEPH/KD AS OPPONENTS: 🔥 40 matchups (24-16, Durant) 🔥 1 WCF series (4-3, Curry) 🔥 Curry: 25.5 PPG, 6.3 APG, 3.8 3PM 🔥 Durant:… pic.twitter.com/jBJkrIxqby — NBA (@NBA) November 11, 2026 Tonight is the 41st time these two have faced each other. Both teams are 8-3, and both are coming off seasons that ended beneath them. The Warriors went 37-45 and lost to Phoenix in the play-in. Houston won 52 games and then fell to the Lakers in the first round with Durant hobbled. Golden State has won eight straight, and its offense ranks second in the league, one spot ahead of Houston’s. KD and Steph’s legacies are tied together for good. They went from playoff rivals in 2016 to teammates in Oakland, where they won two titles and Durant took home both Finals MVPs . In Paris in 2024, with France still threatening an upset, Steph swung the ball to Durant at the top of the key, and KD handed it right back . Steph buried a fadeaway three over Nic Batum and Evan Fournier to put the U.S. up nine with 35 seconds left. As teammates they’ve proven at the highest level how to make sure each other gets the ball when it’s their moment to shine. And nobody can seize the moment like these two hoopers can. A crazy perspective on Curry now is the scoring he packs into the minutes he’s got. He’s averaging 30.6 points, with nights of 44 and 41 already. Through his first seven games, he was scoring 1.04 points per minute , a rate only Wilt Chamberlain, George Gervin, Luka Dončić and James Harden had topped that early in a season. Even Durant has noticed. Back in April he told NBA.com that Steph “ got quicker and faster ,” a terrifying thought for the rest of the league. Stephen Curry: 2015-16: 2026-27: 30.1 PPG 30.6 PPG 50.4% FG 50.3% FG 45.4% 3P 45.7% 3P 90.8% FT 98.7% FT He’s turning 39 in 4 months. pic.twitter.com/apoShDAwma — WarriorsMuse (@WarriorsMuse) November 10, 2026 What’s ice cold about Durant nowadays is his level of control. His scoring is down to 21 a night, the lowest since his rookie year, but the possession still bends around him. He’s a 6-foot-11 sculpture of a jump shot who sits No. 5 on the all-time scoring list, and he just put up 23 points, 12 rebounds and 8 assists on Denver. That’s the problem Golden State has to solve tonight. When Durant has the ball, every defender leans toward him, and teammates like the All-Star Alperen Şengün make you pay for leaning. He’s averaging 21.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.8 assists, and with Houston missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams, even more of the offense will run through those two. Watch whether Draymond can sit on Şengün’s cuts and rolls without giving Durant a clean look. Golden State is still without Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Kristaps Porzingis. This morning’s official report also has Gary Payton II out and Will Richard questionable. Steph owns the playoff edge at 4-3, all from that 2016 comeback. Since Durant left the Warriors, he’s 7-3 against Steph. Houston will take your lunch money in November, but April and May are another story, and the Warriors have five playoff series wins over the Rockets to prove it. Savor this one. Two 38-year-olds are doing things the sport told us were impossible, and we get to watch it on a random Wednesday in November.

stories.title: 'It's forever': Lakers rookie Cameron Carr cherishing first NBA points
stories.summary: After Lakers star Luka Doncic tracks down the game ball to give it to Carr, the rookie guard said he'll have his teammates sign the ball.
stories.detailText: Lakers rookie guard Cameron Carr hangs on the rim after dunking against the Hawks on Monday in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox / Getty Images) The son of former NBA dunk contest runner-up Chris Carr, Lakers rookie Cameron Carr envisioned his first NBA points coming on a lob. When asked before the draft in April, the first-round pick knew that if not on a sky-high alley-oop his first bucket would at least be something athletic. He now gives himself half-credit for calling his shot. The 21-year-old Lakers guard scored his first NBA points on a fastbreak dunk Monday in Atlanta, making the most of his opportunities during the Lakers’ hot start. Carr had two points and three rebounds in seven minutes and 19 seconds in the Lakers’ win over the Atlanta Hawks in the first significant playing time of his professional career. The Lakers, who finish a three-game, four-day road trip in Milwaukee on Wednesday, have the top record in the NBA at 10-2 with a six-game winning streak. Carr helped extend the Lakers’ streak by bolstering a shorthanded lineup against the Hawks. The Lakers needed the rookie Monday when they were without Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain). Three weeks into his NBA career, Carr, the 24th overall pick the Lakers traded up to acquire from the New York Knicks, said he is still nervous any time he subs into a game. Getting the first of what he hopes will be many NBA points helped settle his nerves. Read more: What we’ve learned about the first-place Lakers “Over time it’s only going to grow, it’s only going to get better,” Carr said. “I’m only going to get more and more confident, so every time I get a chance to step out there, just show what I can do and of course show my talents through God’s work.” The 6-foot-5 guard is a skilled scorer and an athletic marvel. He couldn’t even touch the rim when, one summer, he begged his father, who was the runner-up in the 1997 dunk contest to Kobe Bryant, to teach him to dunk. He just needed one summer to master it. Carr set a single-season sophomore scoring record at Baylor last season and his 642 points rank fifth in program history regardless of class. An efficient shooter (37.4% from three in his final college season), Carr also led Baylor with 45 blocked shots. Now in the NBA, defense is still where Carr can improve most, Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Although Carr is a talented offensive player, it is still difficult for young players to find their rhythm with limited playing time, Redick said. The Lakers staff has encouraged Carr to take advantage of stay-ready games against coaches and make the most of G League opportunities to get more reps. Carr had 13 points and four rebounds during the Coachella Valley Lakers’ season opener on Friday. “Just being patient, man,” Carr said of his approach to the beginning of the season, “just putting my head down, working every day, knowing that I can be the best person I can be. And when my time, my name is called, just be ready.” Carr subbed into Monday’s game with 3:35 remaining in the first quarter. The Lakers, trailing by two, soon flipped the game with 13 unanswered points to end the quarter. A steal by Luka Doncic with 1:44 remaining fueled the streak and the star point guard threw an outlet pass to Carr in transition, who collected the ball for an emphatic two-handed dunk. Doncic dished out another assist after the game when he rushed to secure the game ball for Carr. The superstar said he wanted the rookie to remember his first NBA bucket. Cameron Carr said he’s going to ask everyone to sign the game ball from Monday’s game when he scored his first NBA points and keep it in a case. On Luka Doncic chasing it down for him: “That’s big time, especially coming from him. That says a lot about who he is as a person.” pic.twitter.com/eEGrD7VJYy — Thuc Nhi Nguyen (@thucnhi21) November 11, 2026 “That’s big time,” Carr said Wednesday of Doncic’s kind gesture. “Especially coming from him, that says a lot about who he is as a person and how he views this team.” Redick handed the game ball to Carr in the locker room after the win as teammates cheered. Carr broke the team huddle on the word “together.” He plans to have everyone sign the ball before keeping it in a trophy case. “There’s no price on it,” Carr said. “It’s forever.” Lakers sign two-way center The Lakers swapped out two-way centers Tuesday, waiving Lawson Lovering and signing Carson Cooper, the team announced. Both previously played in the Memphis Grizzlies organization and Cooper made one NBA appearance for the Grizzlies after signing a two-way deal with the team. Cooper didn’t become a regular starter in college until his senior season, when he started all 35 games for Michigan State. The four-year Spartan averaged 11.1 points on 58.4% shooting with 7.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists and one block in his final season. Lovering, who signed a two-way deal with the Lakers on Oct. 28, appeared in Lakers blowouts against Miami and Sacramento with a rebound and a block. Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE — Cameron Carr had a prediction for how his first official bucket in the NBA would look. How it actually happened was halfway accurate compared with how he thought it’d go. Cameron Carr’s first NBA bucket came close to how he predicted it would. NBAE via Getty Images Carr said after Wednesday’s shootaround at Fiserv Forum ahead of the Lakers’ game against the Bucks that he was asked what he thought his first NBA bucket would be during the predraft process. The 6-foot-5 wing’s prediction was a lob. Or an athletic play in general. Cameron Carr’s first NBA bucket was a two-handed dunk during Monday’s win over the Hawks. Getty Images The reality: a two-handed fast-break dunk during the first quarter of Monday’s win over the Hawks in Atlanta . “Ended up being an athletic play, so I kind of called it,” Carr said. “Like 50%, halfway called it.” The play helped the former Baylor Bear settle down. “It felt good, get the nerves out, adrenaline out,” Carr said. “I was pretty nervous, still pretty nervous any time I sub in the game, but it’s exciting.” Franchise superstar Luka Dončić secured the game ball for Carr , making sure his young teammate had a souvenir to remember the moment. Luka Doncic secured the game ball for Cameron Carr. NBAE via Getty Images “That’s big time, especially coming from him,” Carr said. “That says a lot about who he is as a person and how he views this team. I would want to do the same thing if I was a vet, grab the ball for the rookie.” Carr already knows what he wants to do with the memento. “I’m going to have everybody sign it, put it in a little trophy case,” he said. “Keep it forever. There’s no price on it — it’s forever.” The win over the Hawks was Carr’s first time being in the rotation since being the No. 24 pick in June’s NBA draft. It also came during a game in which Austin Reaves and Quentin Grimes were sidelined. Before Monday, Carr played a total of four minutes across three NBA games, with his playing time coming at the end of games when the outcome was decided. “Patience has been the key to the game,” Carr said. “It’s always been a part of my career is patience. God’s timing is the best timing. I could want it as bad as I want right now, but maybe it’s not for me right now. And I think sometimes God keeps things from you because maybe you aren’t ready for it. Just being patient, man, just putting my head down, working every day, knowing that I can be the best person I can be. And when my name is called, just be ready.”

stories.summary: The Celtics close out their 4 game road trip with a stop in Toronto to take on the Raptors.
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MA - APRIL 5: RJ Barrett #9 of the Toronto Raptors drives to the basket during the game against the Boston Celtics on April 5, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. They will play in Toronto again on January 31 and twice in Boston on January 25 and February 14. The Celtics won all 4 games against the Raptors last season. They are 77-43 overall, all time, against the Raptors and they are 32-26 all time in games played at Toronto. The Celtics have won their last 5 games against Toronto. The Celtics are playing in the 2nd of back to back games, having played at Philadelphia on Tuesday night. This is the third of 16 back to back sets for the Celtics this season. The Celtics were good in back to back games last season and hopefully, with their depth, it will carry through to this season. They are 1-1 so far on the second night of back to back games. They beat Brooklyn at home in the first and lost to Houston on the road in the second. With their win over the 76ers on Tuesday, the Celtics now are 1st in the East, half a game ahead of Philly. They are 4-2 on the road and 9-1 in their last 10 games. They are 3-0 against Atlantic Division teams. They have won their last 4 games. The Raptors are 6th in the East, 3.5 games behind the Celtics. They are 2-2 at home and 5-5 in their last 10 games. This is their first game against an Atlantic Division rival. They are coming off a loss in their last game. The Raptors made several moves in the offseason. They added Kyle Anderson to the main roster as a free agent and they added Kevin McCullar, Jr, Nate Bittle, and Malachi Smith as 2-Way players. They traded for Kawhi Leonard and they drafted Allen Graves with the 19th pick and Jaden Bradley with the 50th pick. They lost Gradey Dick, Chucky Hepburn, Brandon Ingram, AJ Lawson, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Jonathan Mogbo and Garrett Temple. After this game, the Celtics will return home to face Dallas and Orlando before a West coast trip that takes them through Denver, Sacramento, Golden State, and Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it’s home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. Next they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland. After this game at home, the Raptors play at Philadelphia then home for two games against New York and one against Washington. Then they play one game at Detroit before 3 games at home against Milwaukee, Brooklyn, and Denver. Next they have a 4 game road trip against Houston, San Antonio, Oklahoma City, and Charlotte before a 3 game home stand against San Antonio, Golden State, and Houston. Predicting the starting lineup for this game is tough. The Celtics have been changing the 5th starter on a regular basis and there is no telling who they will start from game to game. In this one, it’s even harder since they are playing in back to back games and Paul George will be out. I’ve listed a possible starting lineup for them with Sam Hauser in place of PG13, but it will likely change. For the Raptors, they have 3 possible starters questionable who are listed as a game time decision so I’ve listed the starters from their game notes, but that may also change. After his big game against the 76ers, Paul George was listed as out for this game due to an illness. The Raptors have 6 players on their injury report at this time. Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Collin Murray-Boyles (illness) are listed as questionable and will be a game time decision. Kawhi Leonard (knee), Scottie Barnes (groin), Trayce Jackson-Davis (illnerss), and Nate Bittle (foot) are listed as out. He is shooting 45.7% from the field and 27.8% from beyond the arc. Against the Celtics he is averaging 20.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 3.9 assists over his career. He has been struggling from the perimeter, but if left open he is very capable of hitting threes so the Celtics need to defend him both in the paint and on the perimeter. Sam Hauser vs Ja’Kobe Walter Walter is averaging 11 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He is shooting 38.7% from the field and 32.8% from beyond the arc. Over his career against the Celtics, he is averaging 8.5 points 2.2 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. I’m guessing that Hauser gets the start in place of Paul George. Honorable Mention Neemias Queta vs Jakob Poeltl Poeltl is averaging 8.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. He is shooting 64.6% from the field with no 3 pointers. Since he isn’t a threat from the perimeter, the Celtics need to keep him out of the paint and off the boards. Keys to the Game Defense – Defense is the most important key to winning. The Celtics are 4th in the league with a defensive rating of 106.3. The Raptors are 14th with a defensive rating of 112.4. The Celtics have played good defense for the most part, but there have been times when they let up on the defensive end and allowed teams to come back from big deficits. They must stay committed to playing tough, lock down defense, especially against a Raptors team that plays good defense themselves. The Celtics must especially defend in the paint as the Raptors are 4th in the league with 52.2 points in the paint per game. Rebound – As with defense, rebounding will always be a key to winning every game. The Celtics are 10th with 45.0 rebounds per game. The Raptors are 25th with 41.4 rebounds per game. The Celtics will need to rebound as a team with players crashing the boards from every position. The Celtics can’t score without the ball and rebounding is a great way to get the ball and to get extra possessions and to also deny the Raptors extra possessions. The Raptors are best in the league with 20.7 second chance points per game. The Celtics need to deny them rebounds to limit those points. Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics are at their best when the ball moves and they make the extra pass. When the ball sticks and players try to do too much, the Celtics struggle. But they have to make careful passes and not get sloppy because the Raptors average 22.3 points off turnovers (2nd) and 16.2 fast break points per game. The Celtics need to be careful with their passes and ball handling because if they aren’t the Raptors will make them pay. Play with Energy and Focus for 48 Minutes – The Celtics must play with effort and energy and they have to play harder than the Raptors for all 4 quarters. The team that plays the hardest and with more energy will usually get the win. They also must stay focused on taking good shots and making them. If the 3’s are falling, they are tough to beat. But, if the 3’s aren’t falling, it can get ugly and so the Celtics need to focus on taking the best shots, whether that means shooting more 3’s or taking the ball into the paint if they aren’t falling. X-Factors On the Road and Fatigue – The Celtics are on the road for the 4th straight game and have to deal with the distractions of travel and going through customs along with playing on an unfamiliar court and in front of hostile fans. They are also playing in the second of back to back games and in the 3rd game in 4 nights. Fatigue may come into play down the stretch. Last Game of Road Trip – This is the final game of a tough 4 game road trip and the 3rd game in 4 nights as well as being the second of back to back games. All of that has a lot going against the Celtics. The final game of a road trip is always a tough game. The Celtics will be tired and looking forward to going home. Also they will be coming down off the high of their emotional win in Philly the night before. Hopefully they can shake all of that off and play well in this game. Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. The Celtics need to adjust to how the refs are calling the game and not allow bad calls or no calls to take away their focus from playing the game. They did a good job of overcoming a 28-5 free throw disadvantage against the 76ers. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid flopping (although Embiid seemed to get away with it), off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws, and illegal screens. They have been especially calling flops and push offs and so the Celtics need to avoid doing both.

stories.title: The Suns need to search for another scorer alongside Booker
stories.summary: Devin Booker needs another high-level scoring option, but Phoenix has limited assets and difficult decisions ahead.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 07: Devin Booker #15 of the Phoenix Suns drives to the basket against Fred VanVleet #5 of the Houston Rockets during the first half of the game at Mortgage Matchup Center on November 07, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the season off to a slow start, many Suns fans have expressed frustration with the team, myself included. Whether it’s how the starting lineup fits, the lack of cohesion on defense, the lack of a second star, or frustration with shooting percentages, there’s something for someone to pick at and be mad about. For a team that was supposed to build on last year’s success, it hasn’t looked that bright just yet. They have shown in spurts that they can be this solid, but ultimately their shortcomings seem to overpower their positives. Injuries to the team’s frontcourt at the start of the year forced the Suns into a situation they may not have been as prepared for, and it has ultimately cost them. Then you add Jordan Goodwin being out and missing his hustle and rebounding, and there seem to be some issues. Especially when you look at the fact that in two games, Devin Booker has dropped over 30 points and the team has lost by a landslide; in this recent game vs. the Spurs and the one last week against the Trail Blazers, Booker was on and showed he can be that number one option for this team. He can hunt his shots, find them, and, most importantly, he is not washed. Sadly, in both of those games, Booker had no one else show up offensively to help him. This is where the main problem comes into play, as the Suns’ owner, Mat Ishbia, wants to win a championship, and one with Booker at the helm. Unfortunately, when your second-highest-paid player is the same position and functions best in the same role as your 1A star, you have a problem, and that is where Jalen Green comes into play. Now it’s not all Green’s fault, since they’re asking him to play a role he’s never played in his career, and he’s not too bad at it. Yes, he turns the ball over a lot when he mishandles it, but he can make some nice passes to create plays. The problem is that since he always has to make the pass, he also wants to hunt his shot when others are out. That doesn’t work for Green, though, because it forces contested looks or shots, disrupting the team’s rhythm. His averages this year clearly show this: his worst in six years. Jalen Green this season: 11.0 PPG 41.8% FG 22.2% 3PT 45.5% FT -55 pic.twitter.com/uMAvT80Lww — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 3, 2026 Can he be a good player? For sure, but it depends on whether he can play a role he won’t succeed in on a team that needs a true playmaker and facilitator. That will not help Booker and has proven to be the case this year. Will the Suns regret trading Green, though? No, because the fit was never going to work with how they’re constructed, with Booker in the same role as Green. So how does one get this second star in Phoenix, you may ask, right? Well, that goal may be one of the bigger obstacles for this team, since they lack draft capital. Remember that 2033 pick that the Suns traded for Miles Bridges? That was the team’s most valuable asset, and yet they traded it the day they could for someone who, at best, would be the third offensive option. Your assets are either Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges, Mark Williams, or Jalen Green. Their value isn’t enough to get you anything relevant for the next step. For everyone clamoring for Kyrie Irving, Anthony Davis, and Darius Garland, those players will cost a decent amount of pick value to acquire. With Green basically looking like a glorified six-man for the Suns in his best role, how would that trade value get boosted enough for other teams to see him as a positive? That is why, sadly, this hunt for that second star may have to wait on Khaman Maluach’s development. The big man has looked solid since moving into his bench role, and with more development this year, he can truly set himself up to take those next steps toward becoming a top-tier big man. This year, it seems like the team is trying to figure out new roles for the players we have and then make a playoff run. The offseason will focus on adding a second star player and freeing up time for this big-man duo to cement themselves as the true starter and backup. At this point, I do think waiting that long is just not going to be beneficial. At this rate, we have seen that the true “second option” cannot be that, given his new role as the point guard. Brooks has to step up, and even though he can do it, the Suns should not be living and dying by his catch-and-shoot three for this season to be impactful. In his best role as the best defender, Brooks should be the third or fourth offensive option. The game plan for the Suns seems tough, but there may be some light at the end of the tunnel. Even though we are just around 10 games in, there are clear issues that need to be addressed before the trade deadline. Some of them are even as early as next week, but time will tell if they make those adjustments or stand pat until they can actually pivot in a direction. With all that said, though, one thing is clear: if the Suns want another chance at a championship with Booker, they need another top-tier scoring option.

stories.title: Darius Acuff frustrated with Kings brutal 1-10 record despite his hot start in the NBA: 'I'm not a loser'
stories.summary: The Kings fell to the Orlando Magic 107-100 on Tuesday night, and now hold one of the worst records in the NBA.
stories.detailText: Darius Acuff Jr. is not happy, and it's easy to understand why. The Sacramento Kings rookie, after the team fell to just 1-10 on the new season with a loss to the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night, is starting to feel the frustrations that come with having one of the worst records in the NBA. "I'm not a loser, so it's not fun," Acuff said, via ESPN . "But like I said, it's an 82-game season, so hopefully something will stick." Acuff finished with 29 points in Tuesday's 107-100 loss to the Magic. He shot 10 of 21 from the field, and had six assists and four rebounds to go with it. Acuff has been having an impressive rookie campaign so far. The 19-year-old, who the Kings selected with the No. 7 overall pick out of Arkansas this past summer, has averaged 26.2 points and 7.3 assists per game this season — both of which are among the top 12 throughout the league. He matched the NBA's single-game rookie 3-point record when he drained nine of them in a loss to the Memphis Grizzlies last month, which was also the most ever made in a contest by a teenager. He's also racked up 288 points through the team's first 11 games of the season, which is the most by a rookie over that span since Michael Jordan's first season in the league in 1984. Jordan had 289 points through his first 11 games. Despite all of that, the Kings aren't winning. They are 0-6 at the Golden 1 Center, and their lone win came on the road against the Dallas Mavericks. They've lost four straight entering Friday's contest against the Portland Trail Blazers. The Kings are currently tied for the worst record in the NBA with the Utah Jazz and Milwaukee Bucks. The Chicago Bulls are also equal in the win column at 1-8. Even though Acuff may be mounting a solid Rookie of the Year campaign, it certainly doesn't feel like things are going well in Sacramento just yet. "I don't know what to do," Acuff said. "I feel like we're trying, everybody as a whole. We're just not coming out with the win. "1-10 just don't sound right."
