stories.title: ‘Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics
stories.summary: Brown will face Boston for the first time Tuesday as the Eastern Conference’s top two teams meet in Philadelphia.
stories.detailText: ‘Let's check the ball up': Jaylen Brown ready for first game against Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Jaylen Brown was asked Sunday whether he and Jayson Tatum had spoken since the former teammates addressed their relationship during the preseason. “No,” Brown said. Does he plan to approach Tatum before Tuesday night’s game at Xfinity Mobile Arena? “I mean, he’s on his side, I’m on my side,” Brown said. “We’re playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win. So it’s nothing to talk about. Let’s check the ball up.” After months of public comments , documentaries and questions about how their partnership ended, the basketball will finally take over. Brown will face Boston for the first time since the Celtics traded him to Philadelphia for Paul George and four future draft assets in July. He spent his first 10 NBA seasons in Boston, played nine alongside Tatum and helped the Celtics win the 2024 championship, earning Finals MVP honors. Tuesday’s 8 p.m. game on NBC will also bring together the top two teams in the Eastern Conference. The Sixers are 9-2. Boston, riding a three-game winning streak, is 8-2 and sits a half-game behind Philadelphia. “Another good opportunity for our team to be able to show what we’re made of,” Brown said. “I’m looking forward to it. Big-time matchup, two heavyweights in the East. Let’s get it.” A reunion without the small talk Brown has not hidden his appreciation for Boston, even as more has emerged about the deterioration of his relationship with Tatum and the organization. “I love Boston,” he said Sunday. “Boston’s a great city. A lot of people I developed relationships with, you know what I mean? But I’m just focused on what’s in front of me right now. And that’s the most important thing.” He also acknowledged everything that accompanies an abrupt end to a decade with one organization. “Decisions were made,” Brown said. “It’s life. It’s business. Move on. It’s OK. … It’s emotions. You’ve got to pack up and move your stuff. Your family’s got to pack up and move. But it’s life. It’s happened to numerous amounts of people, myself included. “So I just look forward to being able to build with my team over here, trying to make the best of my situation.” Brown faced the Celtics during the preseason, but Tuesday will be the first meeting that counts. He said he did not know whether that would introduce emotions that were absent during the exhibition schedule. “We’ll see how I feel when we get out there,” Brown said. “As of now, I’ve got no emotion toward nothing. So I’m just ready to go.” Tatum was similarly restrained after Boston’s 117-97 victory over Milwaukee on Sunday. “It’s another game on the schedule,” Tatum said. “It’s the Celtics versus the Sixers. In the words of Brad Stevens, they all count as one.” Tatum called the Sixers “an incredible group” with a “great coaching staff,” but declined to add to the discussion surrounding his relationship with Brown. “Drama gets clicks and views,” he said. “That’s not my thing.” CBS Sports reported Tatum’s full comments Sunday night. Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla was even more concise. “It’ll be fun,” Mazzulla said. “It’ll be a good atmosphere.” The other side of the trade Brown is not the only centerpiece of the July deal who will face his former team. George has settled quickly into Boston’s lineup, averaging 20.4 points and supplying the high-volume outside shooting the Celtics have long prioritized. He scored 27 points and made five three-pointers Sunday as Boston beat Milwaukee for its third consecutive victory. The Celtics have not needed George to duplicate everything Brown provided. He has fit alongside Tatum, Derrick White and Boston’s returning core as another willing shooter and versatile defender. Tatum is averaging 27.1 points, six rebounds and 7.8 assists. His playmaking has been especially important for a team that replaced Brown’s downhill pressure with more shooting and ball movement. Boston enters Tuesday ranked third in offensive rating and fourth in defensive rating. It is one of two NBA teams currently inside the top five on both ends of the floor. The Celtics have also made 15.6 three-pointers per game, the second-highest average in the league. They set an NBA Cup record by hitting 24 against Charlotte on Friday, then made 18 more Sunday in Milwaukee. That presents a clear challenge for a Sixers defense that has generally performed well but has occasionally surrendered clean perimeter looks after committing extra help toward the ball. Tatum, George, White, Payton Pritchard and Sam Hauser can all punish late rotations. What the matchup could reveal The Sixers have reached 9-2 without depending upon the same formula every night. Tyrese Maxey leads them at 26.9 points per game. Brown is averaging 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds and four assists while shooting 47.7 percent from the field and 39.2 percent from three. Joel Embiid and LeBron James have supplied scoring, passing and defensive flexibility around them. Brown has repeatedly described the team as unfinished despite its record. “From our perspective, it’s been some growing pains for sure, even though we’ve been able to win,” he said. “The result, we’re not so much fixated on the result. It’s more so about the process, and we’ve got to improve our process and our mentality to creating a winning environment.” Boston should provide the clearest early measure of that process. The Celtics play considerably slower than the Sixers, but their half-court execution has been more efficient. Philadelphia will want to create turnovers and run before Boston can set its defense. The Celtics will attempt to control the pace, generate three-pointers and make the Sixers execute against a defense that has yet to allow an opposing player to score 30 points this season. There is also the unavoidable Brown matchup. Boston could use Tatum, George and White against him at different points, giving the Celtics several defenders capable of absorbing his drives without immediately sending help. Nick Nurse expects Brown to bring something extra, even if Brown has publicly downplayed the emotional component. “It’s going to be very different for him,” Nurse said. “I think probably a little bit of emotion in there, too, but also I think he’s going to be very motivated to play.” What the odds say Boston’s rotation is healthy entering the matchup. Two-way guard Devin Carter is out because of an illness. Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti remain out for the Sixers. Adem Bona could return after missing Sunday’s contest. The betting market views the matchup as essentially a toss-up. Monday afternoon listings had the spread moving between Boston minus-1.5 and Philadelphia minus-1.5, depending on the sportsbook, with the total at 215.5. That fits the larger picture. Philadelphia owns the East’s best record. Boston has the conference’s strongest point differential and has outscored opponents by 10.7 points per game. The surrounding conversation will center on Brown and Tatum until the opening tip. Brown does not intend to contribute any ceremonial small talk. “He’s on his side,” Brown said. “I’m on my side.” Then they will check the ball up.

stories.title: Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to ‘a regular game'
stories.summary: After two seasons with the Sixers, Paul George has returned to Philadelphia.
stories.detailText: Back in Philadelphia with Celtics, Paul George looks forward to ‘a regular game' originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Paul George’s presence back in town was one of the many swirling morning storylines at Xfinity Mobile Arena. For good reason, former Celtics teammates Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum will draw immense attention Tuesday night. After all, Brown has said there “might be a little lamb chops with some gravy” between the two, if not a full-blown beef. But George’s return to Philadelphia is more than a tiny subplot. Following two seasons in Philadelphia, he was the centerpiece of the Sixers’ summer trade package to acquire Brown. George told reporters before the Celtics’ shootaround that it feels like “a regular game.” “Had I been here eight, nine, 10 years, different story,” he said. “I was here two years. Obviously, we didn’t have the best of luck or had a great, I think, partnership in terms of my ability to stay healthy and on the floor. So that kind of played into a lot of it. “But obviously, it’s a tremendous fan base, a great sports town to play in. So that was appreciated. There’s no ill will for me. It’ll be fun to just compete. And outside of that, it’s a normal game.” Paul George at Celtics shootaround: pic.twitter.com/DWlYfpKfzE — Noah Levick (@NoahLevick) November 10, 2026 The 36-year-old George indeed had trouble staying available for sustained stretches as a Sixer. He dealt with a variety of injuries and served a 25-game suspension last season for violating the NBA’s anti-drug policy. George did play well on both ends of the floor for much of the 2026 playoffs. He helped the Sixers come back to win a seven-game first-round series against the Celtics in historic fashion . The nine-time All-Star also brought a veteran steadiness to the Sixers’ locker room and was glad to mentor younger players like VJ Edgecombe. “Just his routine … even when he got hot, he didn’t try to force it,” Jabari Walker said Tuesday morning. “His game was smooth and I think that’s how he is as a person, just not forcing anything and having a calm energy.” George has certainly enjoyed his early days as a Celtic. Through nine games, he’s averaged 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists and 2.3 steals while shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range. Boston will enter Tuesday night’s matchup second in the Eastern Conference standings at 8-2, the Sixers first at 9-2. “I’ve been kind of blown away,” George said. “I think it exceeded my expectations since being in Boston. You never know how much culture is involved and how much culture changes your outlook on things and the effect it has mentally, physically, just being in an environment … and the culture that Boston presents. “So I’ve been thrilled. I’ve been playing some of my best basketball of late, and just been enjoying grinding it out with these guys out here. It’s a fun style of play and I can’t talk (enough) about just the thrill, the happiness and the excitement and joy that it has brought being here.” He was asked what sort of reception he expects from Sixers fans. “Not sure,” George said. “In some ways, I helped land them a future piece for them. So with that, not sure how the reception would be.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup
stories.summary: The Sixers fell to their second loss of the season on Friday night in Cleveland.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers couldn’t rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers. They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4. The Sixers’ top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17). The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley. The Sixers’ injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury. With Friday’s loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat. The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland: Nightmare start for Embiid, Sixers After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam. The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers’ Oct. 22 win over Cleveland , they were many levels below their best in the first quarter. The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers’ chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid’s larger problem was that he couldn’t hit any sort of shot besides free throws. He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds. Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he’s now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that’s bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season. Of course, it’s notable that Embiid’s been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We’ll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out. James didn’t play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers. As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc. Edgecombe shrugs off foul trouble Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers’ rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures. With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland’s lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass. Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals. Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers’ comeback push. Cavs polish it off in 2nd half The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk. With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons , Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game. Still, the Sixers’ offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points. Embiid didn’t play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He’s had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career , back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors. Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they’d hit speed bumps throughout the year. They’ll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

stories.title: Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown called the Sixers' blowout defeat to the Celtics “humbling.”
stories.detailText: Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night. Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena. “We’ve just got to get better,” Brown said. “Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one.” Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer. As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum , Brown didn’t have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front. The pregame moment between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. 📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/P4iclUnqZ5 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) November 11, 2026 “I’m just focused on doing what’s best for my team,” Brown said. “Everything else … to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight.” Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers. The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating , 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage. “I think that we’ve got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “And I don’t think it’s because they’re shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they’re shots we want them to take. So I think they’ll continue to take ‘em and I’m pretty sure those will even out into their career averages.” Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent). The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers’ home opener back on Oct. 22. “It’s a work in progress,” Embiid said. “I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I’m probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I’m so used to having to create for myself, so it’s a little bit different. “But I think I’m slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn’t even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it’s just about taking what’s in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It’s going to get there at some point.” Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team’s defense has “slacked off a little bit” in recent games. “I don’t really look at the record,” he said. “I just look at the process of, ‘Are we getting better every day?’ We can always do a better job at all phases of the game.” Boston’s now first in the East at 9-2. “They’re one of the top teams in the league and they’ve been together for a while,” Brown said. “We’ve got a lot to work on over here, so we’ve got to get to work.” The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia. They’ll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again. “I was looking forward to this,” Brown said. “I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one.”

stories.title: Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors
stories.summary: The Sixers listed both Joel Embiid and LeBron James as questionable for their game against the Raptors.
stories.detailText: Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers listed both Joel Embiid and LeBron James as questionable for their Thursday night game vs. the Raptors. As has been the case on previous early-season injury reports, James’ official listing was “low back/sciatica management” and Embiid’s was “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” While Thursday’s contest isn’t part of a back-to-back, it’s the sort of situation in which the Sixers have load management matters in mind for the 32-year-old Embiid and 41-year-old James. They’ll host the Pacers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET and then visit the Nets the following night. James logged 29 minutes Tuesday in the 9-3 Sixers’ loss to the Celtics and Embiid went 31. Embiid said postgame that he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter, but he was fine to play the second half. With the Raptors facing Boston on Wednesday night, Toronto’s complete injury report won’t be available until Thursday afternoon. The Raptors announced Tuesday that superstar Kawhi Leonard will be sidelined for at least one more week because of his left knee injury. Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) will all remain out for the Sixers against the Raptors.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers lose 1st Brown vs. Tatum matchup, George scores 36
stories.summary: Round 1 of the new-look Sixers vs. the new-look Celtics decisively went Boston’s way on Tuesday night.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers lose 1st Brown vs. Tatum matchup, George scores 36 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Round 1 of the new-look Sixers vs. the new-look Celtics decisively went Boston’s way on Tuesday night. In the first meeting between the teams since the July trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and Paul George to Boston , the Celtics earned a 123-101 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The Sixers dropped to 9-3 and the Celtics improved to 9-2. George was the game’s brightest star, scoring 36 points on 14-for-22 shooting. Jayson Tatum added 21 points. Tyrese Maxey’s 24 points led the Sixers. Brown was hampered by foul trouble in his heavily anticipated first outing against Tatum . He posted 13 points, five rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes. The Sixers will host the Raptors on Thursday night. Here are observations on their blowout loss to the Celtics: Brown vs. Tatum takes center stage To no one’s surprise, Brown and Tatum guarded each other to open the night. VJ Edgecombe defended a former teammate in George , who scored Boston’s first four points with a pair of pure jumpers. On the other end, Maxey made the Sixers’ first three field goals. Judging by volume, the home fans cared most about the much-scrutinized Brown vs. Tatum matchup. The crowd was excited early when Brown snagged a steal and then dished to Maxey for a fast-break three-pointer. The fans also dialed up the noise when Brown sized up Tatum in isolation. He wound up dribbling the ball off his foot and out of bounds. Tatum pointed to signal it was Celtics ball. Boston’s star forward had a productive first quarter, posting 11 points. He scored an easy two when he used a back screen to break free from Brown and convert a layup that put the Celtics up 11-7. Boston began 9 for 12 from the floor as a team. As for Brown, he sat shortly after being called for his second foul with 6:48 left in the first quarter. Rough going for Sixers from long distance Brown re-entered at the start of the second quarter. The Sixers still struggled to eat into Boston’s lead. A Sam Hauser triple extended the Celtics’ advantage to 12 points. There was some audible frustration in the building after Brown missed two free throws on the next possesion. The Sixers’ deficit hit 16 points on a Hugo Gonzalez jumper. Meanwhile, the Sixers missed 12 of their first 14 three-point tries. While some of those shots were open looks that simply didn’t go down, the Sixers also rushed up several contested jumpers before they made Boston’s defense do serious work. In the bigger picture, it wouldn’t be remotely surprising if shooting stands out as a weak area for the Sixers come the trade deadline. They entered the game ranked 27th in the NBA in three-point frequency outside of garbage time and 22nd in three-point accuracy, according to Cleaning the Glass. George and Tatum lead the way Joel Embiid (16 points, six rebounds) had an injury scare late in the second quarter when he fell hard after missing a layup in transition. He rose gingerly and limped through the final 30 seconds or so of the first half. The Sixers’ star big man was fine to start the third quarter and even drained a long-overdue three on the opening possession. He’d been in a terrible outside shooting slump (3 for 32 from deep on the season) before that shot. Brown’s foul trouble persisted. He picked up his fourth personal with 10:40 to go in the third quarter. The Sixers stormed back without him and their defense played a large role. After LeBron James rumbled in for a layup, Dean Wade stonewalled Payton Pritchard on the perimeter to force a shot-clock violation. Wade later canned a three to even the contest at 76-all. The Celtics responded and Tatum led the charge. His third-quarter exploits included a highlight slam on James and a top-of-the-key three to build Boston’s lead back up to nine points. Pritchard buried a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter and the Celtics’ advantage kept growing. George celebrated a triple that stretched his team’s lead to 100-82. The Sixers’ spirits were considerably lower as they headed to their bench for a timeout. As a Sixer, George only had one higher-scoring game (39 points) than his performance Tuesday. George and Tatum were each excellent in Philadelphia. Outside of Maxey, who finished 8 for 12 from the field, the Sixers didn’t receive similar games from their stars. Brown will be back in Boston on Jan. 21 when the Sixers visit the Celtics. He’ll try to even the score.

stories.title: LeBron Log No. 4: A courtside sip, 16,000 makes and Cleveland's welcome
stories.summary: James sampled a fan’s wine, reached an unprecedented scoring milestone and experienced Cleveland’s full emotional range.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log No. 4: A courtside sip, 16,000 makes and Cleveland's welcome originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James’ latest week with the Sixers included a sip of a stranger’s wine, yet another number no NBA player had reached and a return to the city where his career began. It also included his worst performance with Philadelphia, followed less than 48 hours later by his highest-scoring game with the team. Welcome to the fourth edition of the LeBron Log. A SIP OF PHILLY No chronicle of James’ first season in Philadelphia could omit the time he helped himself to a fan’s wine during a game. James chased Tyrese Maxey’s transition pass into the stands during the third quarter of the Sixers’ Nov. 2 win over the Bulls. He collided with Philadelphia native Troy Clemons, spilled some of Clemons’ wine and sampled what had landed on his arm. The interaction received its own story on our site , and deservedly so. It also belongs in the Log. Clemons did not keep the cup as a souvenir. He threw it away and got another drink. James returned to the court and later broke into a dance after scoring over the 6-foot-1 Tre Jones. The wine clip generated millions of views across social media and became the defining image from an otherwise ordinary 19-point Sixers victory. The following night in Detroit, James offered a broader explanation for why Philadelphia has already looked comfortable together. “We’ve got a good team,” James said. “Guys vibe with one another. Guys like each other. Guys enjoy being around each other. That has a lot to do with it, too. It makes the game a lot easier when you enjoy being around people.” Eleven games into his Sixers career, James appears to be doing exactly that. Just interviewed Troy Clemons, the Sixers fan whose wine LeBron took a sip of during tonight’s game And no, he did not save the cup https://t.co/U3oV3Y2ArH pic.twitter.com/vWzkhGJxmH — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 3, 2026 16,000 AND COUNTING James arrived in Detroit two baskets away from another unprecedented number. His second field goal against the Pistons made him the first player in NBA history to reach 16,000 regular-season field goals . James finished the Sixers’ 112-106 victory with 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. The near-triple-double helped Philadelphia improve to 8-1 and avenge its only loss of the season. Kareem Abdul-Jabbar ranks second in league history with 15,837 made field goals. Karl Malone is a distant third at 13,528. James is the only active player with more than 12,000. His scoring record has long been secure. James passed Abdul-Jabbar in career points in February 2023 and later overtook him in made baskets. The round number in Detroit still illustrated the distance he has created between himself and every other scorer. James began his career by making 5,361 field goals across seven seasons with Cleveland. He added 3,510 in Miami, returned to make 3,691 more for the Cavaliers and made another 3,421 during eight years with the Lakers. Basket No. 16,000 belonged to Philadelphia. The Sixers’ 8-1 start also carried a notable James connection. Each of his previous four teams to begin a season at least 7-1 reached the NBA Finals. James was not ready to entertain that conversation in early November. “It’s too early to be talking about the Finals and things of that nature,” he said. “We’ve got to continue to buy into what we want to do.” HELL, HEAVEN AND EVERYTHING BETWEEN Two nights later, James returned to the place where nearly half of those 16,000 baskets were made. His first game in Cleveland as a Sixer brought out jerseys from every stop of his career. Cavaliers colors filled Rocket Arena alongside Heat black, Lakers purple and the Sixers’ throwback look. James received a warm ovation when he was introduced last among Philadelphia’s starters. When he checked out late in the fourth quarter, with the result decided, the crowd stood for him again. James has experienced both ends of Cleveland’s emotional range. He returned as a member of the Heat on Dec. 2, 2010, to one of the most hostile receptions in NBA history. Six years later, he delivered the Cavaliers their first championship and ended Cleveland’s 52-year major professional sports title drought. “I’ve seen the depths of hell when it comes to a reception here, all the way to the heavens above,” James said. “Anything in between is easy money.” The reception fell somewhere in the middle. His performance landed much closer to the bottom. James finished with eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, three assists and six turnovers in the Sixers’ 119-95 loss. It was his first single-digit performance in Cleveland since he scored three points against the Rockets on Dec. 30, 2004. He had scored at least 10 points in 396 consecutive regular-season games in the city. The run covered his first stint with the Cavaliers, every visit as an opponent and his entire second tenure with the organization. It ended during his first trip back in a Sixers uniform. “I definitely did not feel in a good rhythm offensively,” James said. “A couple of them were careless. A couple of them were just trying to make the right play and not being successful with it.” It was only the 10th single-digit regular-season game of James’ 1,630-game career. He still took time afterward to consider what an eventual jersey retirement in Cleveland could represent. “The journey from being an 18-year-old rookie, to leading a franchise to a championship,” James said. “And everything in between.” THE PASS HE HAD TO WATCH AGAIN James did not carry the rough night into Chicago. Less than 48 hours after struggling in Cleveland, he scored a season-high 22 points in the Sixers’ 127-121 victory over the Bulls. Thirteen came during the second quarter, when James helped Philadelphia turn an early deficit into a halftime lead. His first basket produced another milestone. James entered Sunday trailing Abdul-Jabbar’s 1,895 points for the most scored against the Bulls in NBA history . His first-quarter three-pointer moved him into the lead. He ended the afternoon with 1,916. The most interesting play from his night was a pass. With the Sixers ahead by four and 2:20 remaining, James drove into the paint. Three Chicago defenders collapsed toward him. Maxey stood between the left wing and corner, but even he did not believe James could see him. James fired the ball through the defense. Maxey sidestepped Isaac Okoro and made the three-pointer, pushing Philadelphia’s lead to seven. After his postgame interview, James pulled out his phone and watched the play again. “He didn’t think I saw him,” James called out from his locker as reporters asked Maxey about the possession. Maxey acknowledged that he had positioned himself to rebound because he expected James to shoot. “Honestly, I was like this,” Maxey said, raising his hands. “I thought he was about to shoot a layup.” James has spent the opening weeks of the season teaching his new teammates to expect the unexpected pass. “You’ve got to become a wide receiver or a catcher at that point,” Maxey said. “You never know when you’re going to get the ball. “And that’s good.”

stories.title: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return
stories.summary: PG-13, the former Sixer, poured in 36 points, then explained the baseline exchange that gave his return an R rating.
stories.detailText: Paul George flips the script — and the bird — in Philadelphia return originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia PG-13 was rated R in his return to Philadelphia. The middle finger Paul George directed toward one baseline fan only reinforced that rating. Tuesday night was expected to revolve around Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum sharing an NBA court as opponents for the first time. Instead, the other headliner in the summer’s blockbuster trade stole the show. George scored a game-high 36 points in Boston’s 123-101 win over the Sixers. He shot 14 for 22 from the floor, made six of his 11 three-point attempts and scored 14 consecutive Boston points in the fourth quarter. The game was tied at 79 with 3:19 remaining in the third quarter. Boston outscored Philadelphia 44-22 from that point forward. The Celtics went nine minutes and 20 seconds without making a two-point field goal during the second half. Instead, they made nine consecutive field goals from three, the second-longest such streak by a Sixers opponent over the last 30 seasons. Payton Pritchard opened the fourth with consecutive threes. George followed with eight straight points, helping the Celtics begin the quarter on a 14-0 run that turned a competitive game into a rout. George’s return carried a complicated history. His two seasons with the Sixers were repeatedly interrupted by injuries, but he also played a significant role in their most memorable playoff run in years. Last spring, George helped the Sixers overcome a 3-1 deficit to eliminate Boston in seven games. He averaged 17.4 points and shot 55 percent from three during the series. Tyrese Maxey was happy to see his former teammate Tuesday, even if he disliked what followed. “It was good to see Paul,” Maxey said. “I love him, love his family. … He gave us everything he had while he was here. We know what he did in the playoffs last year. Great person, great family, and we’ll see him again.” Maxey then added one important qualifier. “I wanted him to score zero points.” George instead scored from nearly everywhere. “He had some open threes. He had some pull-up threes. He had some middies,” Maxey said. “He played within the game, too. That’s what Paul does. He plays within the game. He takes what the defense gives him, and we gave him too many open looks tonight. “PG, we know what PG does. We shouldn’t even be allowing him to get up 11 threes, and that’s on us.” Nick Nurse watched George attack the Sixers in several ways. “He really had it going,” Nurse said. “He’d post up, and-one, fallaways. He went down the lane, high archer off the glass, and-one. He scored in about every way he could tonight.” George heard boos during his return and said the arena carried the atmosphere, though not quite the intensity, of a playoff game. “This building can be very electric as well,” George said. “It was fun. It was fun to play in this environment.” One interaction extended beyond the usual reception for a returning player. During a stoppage, the ball rolled toward a fan seated along the baseline. George said the fan looked directly at him before dropping the ball instead of returning it. “There was a fan being an a–,” George said. “The ball rolled to him. He looked me dead in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if I’m a dog to go fetch or go get it, instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do. “And so, yeah, then I rolled him a middle finger in return.”

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: Lauri Markkanen injury update could have major fallout for Utah Jazz
stories.summary: The Utah Jazz got a sobering injury update for star Lauri Markkanen, adding to their problems during a disastrous start to the 2026-27 NBA season.
stories.detailText: The Utah Jazz hoped to be part of the Western Conference playoff race this season after years of rebuilding. But those plans have gone horribly awry during the opening few weeks of the 2026-27 NBA campaign , and getting back on track just became even more difficult after a sobering update involving star Lauri Markkanen . Markkanen is expected to miss at least a month of action, the Jazz announced on Nov. 11 , after suffering a right hand injury during the team's loss to the Dallas Mavericks last Friday . Markkanen is the latest key Jazz player to be sidelined, and the mounting absences have left Utah tied for the NBA's worst record at 1-10 entering Wednesday's matchup against the Orlando Magic . Here's more on Markkanen's injury status and what it means for the Jazz's hopes of reaching the postseason. NBA: Kon Knueppel's latest injury setback could be crushing blow for Hornets Lauri Markkanen injury update Markkanen has been diagnosed with two nondisplaced fractures in his right hand and will be re-evaluated in four weeks. The good news is a nondisplaced fracture is considered less severe than a displaced fracture, in which the bones are no longer in proper alignment. A non-displaced fracture generally doesn't require surgery. The 29-year-old forward had already been playing through a sprained right wrist as the Jazz were hit hard with injuries during the first month of the NBA season. An initial X-ray did not reveal the fracture, according to ESPN , but Markkanen underwent scans that revealed more damage after returning to Utah in recent days. Why Lauri Markkanen's injury could be devastating for Jazz The Jazz were already teetering to start the 2026-27 season because of injuries, and they've lost 10 of their first 11 games. Utah watched Jaren Jackson Jr. go down for at least two months with a knee injury , while center Jusuf Nurkic has yet to appear in a game this season because of a toe injury. Guard Keyonte George has also been dealing with a sprained ankle and did not play in Tuesday's loss to the Miami Heat. That leaves rookie Darryn Peterson as the only player from the Jazz's expected Opening Night starting lineup currently available entering Wednesday. Utah was already struggling with Markkanen in the lineup, and losing its most reliable offensive weapon only makes an uphill climb steeper. His ability to score at all three levels, stretch defenses and create matchup problems is central to everything the Jazz want to do offensively. The timing is just brutal. A team that entered the season hoping to take a step forward is suddenly staring at the possibility of another year buried near the bottom of the Western Conference. The injury could also create bigger-picture questions for the franchise. The Jazz resisted opportunities to trade Markkanen when his value was arguably at its peak, believing he would be the centerpiece of their return to contention. Now, with Utah off to a disastrous start and its roster ravaged by injuries, the mission is simply to keep the season from slipping away before Markkanen can return. If this season ends as disastrously as it has started, the Jazz could revisit assumptions that have guided their moves to this point, including whether their current timeline and roster construction around Markkanen remain the right path forward. Lauri Markkanen stats Markkanen was averaging 18 points and 6.8 rebounds per game through eight games for the Jazz this season. He was shooting just 38.9% from the floor, which is the worst mark of his career. Markkanen averaged 26.7 points on 47.7% shooting during the 2025-26 season. teamStories.detailText: The NBA season is starting to take shape as the holiday window approaches. The San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are once again surging early, but their Western Conference counterparts the Los Angeles Lakers have arguably been the most impressive team in a competitive West. The Lakers are fueled by Luka Doncic 's historic start, which has featured 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game. In the East, the new-look Philadelphia 76ers seem like they've been playing together for years, as LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have hit the ground running with their new teammates. They're tailed tightly by their offseason trade partners, the Boston Celtics , who seemingly haven't missed a beat with new faces around Jayson Tatum . In this week's Power Rankings, our ESPN insiders rank where each team stands, per usual, and also highlight each team's best newcomer over the first few weeks of the season. Which players are vaulting their teams up the standings? Find out in this week's Power Rankings. Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28 | Nov. 4 Jump to a team: ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS 1. San Antonio Spurs 2026-27 record: 9-2 Previous ranking: 5 Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 11), vs. GS (Nov. 13), @ UTAH (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Tarris Reed Jr . Drafted 26th in 2026, Tarris Reed Jr. knew earning minutes as a rookie in San Antonio would be difficult, even after he gave French phenom Victor Wembanyama buckets, according to sources, in the early days of open gym over the summer. Reed is averaging just 5.3 minutes per game, but the Spurs' brass has been impressed with the rookie's preparedness every time his number is called. San Antonio is thin at center, and veteran backup Luke Kornet has struggled. That could lead to more minutes for Reed as the season progresses. -- Mike C. Wright 2. Los Angeles Lakers 2026-27 record: 10-2 Previous ranking: 7 Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 11), @ PHX (Nov. 15), vs. CHA (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: C Walker Kessler After recording one of the most memorable debuts imaginable -- when he scored 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 from the field in a win -- Kessler has continued to have a major impact. The 7-2 center has been durable, playing in all 12 of L.A.'s games, and averaging a career high in points (14.9) while shooting 69.1% from the field, with 10.8 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He has also played north of 30 minutes per game while averaging only 2.9 fouls, which is paramount for a Lakers roster without a go-to big man to back him up. -- Dave McMenamin 3. Oklahoma City Thunder 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 10 Next games: @ POR (Nov. 11), @ LAC (Nov. 13), @ SAC (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Aday Mara Rookie center Aday Mara, selected with the No. 12 pick courtesy of the LA Clippers , has made an instant impact in Oklahoma City. The 7-foot-3 big man entered the league as an elite rim protector, ranking fifth in the NBA with 1.9 blocks per game. Mara also has a soft touch in the paint and intriguing potential as a passer. He ranks fifth among rookies in rebounding (5.9 per game) and is also averaging 8.1 points on 62.5% shooting over 19 minutes per game. -- Tim MacMahon 4. Philadelphia 76ers 2026-27 record: 9-3 Previous ranking: 3 Next games: vs. TOR (Nov. 12), vs. IND (Nov. 15), @ BKN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Jaylen Brown Brown has said that this is Tyrese Maxey's team, but as of late, it's starting to look like his, as well. He had his best stretch as a Sixer on the team's recent road trip, scoring 30 points in a win over Detroit and 29 points in a win over the Chicago Bulls . "He's something we really needed," Maxey said. -- Kris Rhim 5. Boston Celtics 2026-27 record: 9-2 Previous ranking: 4 Next games: @ TOR (Nov. 11), vs. DAL (Nov. 15), vs. ORL (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Paul George George set the tone for what this season would be on opening night, breaking the franchise record for the most points in a debut with 38. Since then, he has remained a seamless fit in Boston, becoming one of the team's best wing defenders and a reliable second option on offense as the Celtics have jumped out to the second-best record in the East. "On and off the court he's been great," coach Joe Mazzulla said. -- Rhim 6. Minnesota Timberwolves 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 11 Next games: vs. DAL (Nov. 12), vs. CHI (Nov. 14), vs. POR (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G LaMelo Ball The Timberwolves should be ecstatic with the early returns from their summer trade for Ball, who quickly forged a dynamic partnership with Anthony Edwards . Even after Edwards was sidelined by knee surgery, Ball has kept Minnesota's offense in the top 10 and is on pace to be the franchise's first player to average at least six assists since D'Angelo Russell in 2022-23. Meanwhile, the Hornets' offensive efficiency has plummeted from fifth last season to 30th this season after trading Ball in June. No takebacks. -- Ben Golliver 7. Houston Rockets 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 1 Next games: vs. GS (Nov. 11), vs. UTAH (Nov. 13), @ WAS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Marcus Smart Veteran guard Marcus Smart is not only reliable for coach Ime Udoka but also familiar with him from their time together with the Celtics. Most of all, Smart gives the Rockets another steady ball handler and tenacious defender capable of starting whenever Fred VanVleet is forced to rest on the second night of back-to-backs, as he continues to recover from last year's ACL surgery. A former NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Smart plays with the intelligence and toughness that Udoka covets and provides veteran leadership alongside VanVleet and Kevin Durant . -- Wright 8. Detroit Pistons 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 2 Next games: @ WAS (Nov. 12), @ MIA (Nov. 14), @ SAS (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: F John Collins It was a bit of a slow start for Collins, who signed as a free agent to replace veteran Tobias Harris . Collins fits more what the Pistons want to be, with his athleticism and shooting as complements to Jalen Duren 's interior presence. However, with Duren out with a hamstring injury, it forced Collins to be paired with Paul Reed , which has been a bit clunky. When J.B. Bickerstaff removed Reed from the first five and went small against the Wizards, it opened things up for Collins -- he scored a season-high 24 points and added 10 rebounds in a 122-111 win Monday night. -- Vincent Goodwill 9. Golden State Warriors 2026-27 record: 8-3 Previous ranking: 12 Next games: @ HOU (Nov. 11), @ SAS (Nov. 13), @ NO (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Yaxel Lendeborg During one of his unfiltered livestreams this summer, Lendeborg -- the outspoken No. 11 pick -- predicted he would average around 15 points, six rebounds and four assists as a rookie. It felt overly ambitious at the time. It appears he might've been shorting himself. Through his first 11 games, Lendeborg is averaging 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists. The scoring punch has been particularly surprising and important for the surging 8-3 Warriors. Lendeborg is making better than 44% of his 5.5 attempted 3s per game and has gained enough trust from Steve Kerr that the coach is putting the basketball in the rookie's hands to make decisions down the stretch of close games. -- Anthony Slater 10. New York Knicks 2026-27 record: 6-4 Previous ranking: 17 Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 11), @ IND (Nov. 13), @ TOR (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Andre Drummond At times it has appeared like Drummond has been out of place, with Mike Brown pulling Drummond abruptly in the middle of games for not getting back on defense and trying his hand with James Wiseman instead. But one thing that cannot be denied is Drummond's effect on the glass. The Knicks were supposed to suffer a drop-off as one of the best offensive rebounding teams after Mitchell Robinson departed to Boston. But per 36 minutes, Drummond has averaged over eight offensive rebounds to help the Knicks remain a top-three team in that category. And Brown has complemented Drummond's screen-roll defense recently, noting his physicality. -- Goodwill 11. Portland Trail Blazers 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 8 Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 11), @ SAC (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Damian Lillard Portland's best newcomer is actually an old friend in Lillard, who is doing his best to make Rip City forget that he was traded to the Bucks in 2023 and missed last season with an Achilles injury. Lillard, 36, is averaging 19.4 points and 4.4 assists, and he has made fast friends with All-Star wing Deni Avdija . The Blazers boast an excellent plus-9.4 net rating when Avdija and Lillard, their two leading scorers, share the court. -- Golliver 12. Denver Nuggets 2026-27 record: 5-4 Previous ranking: 15 Next games: @ MEM (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 14), vs. PHX (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Trevon Brazile The Nuggets remain in a perpetual search for lineup combinations that can survive in the minutes either Nikola Jokic or the scorching Jamal Murray are off the floor. Through nine games, they're minus-15 in Jokic's bench time and minus-29 in Murray's. But within that, in their latest search for depth pieces after Peyton Watson 's departure this past summer, they've received encouraging contributions from Brazile and Bryce Hopkins -- both second-rounders from the 2026 draft. Brazile is a 6-10 wing with a 7-4 wingspan, flashing early as a rebounder and a defensive disruptor in a few of Denver's wins. He's averaging 20.3 minutes, a number that might rise as the season progresses. -- Slater 13. Memphis Grizzlies 2026-27 record: 7-3 Previous ranking: 6 Next games: vs. DEN (Nov. 11), @ NO (Nov. 13), vs. @BKN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Cameron Boozer Rookie Cameron Boozer, the third pick of the 2026 draft, is already surprising some opponents with his unexpected agility and scoring prowess. "I had no clue he could move the way he moves, also that he could shoot the way he shoots," said Golden State center Draymond Green on "The Draymond Green Show" podcast. With Isaiah Stewart out due to a right knee bone bruise, Boozer is also having to showcase his versatility by sliding over from his natural power forward spot to center. "We are featuring him in a lot of different sets," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo said. -- Wright 14. Atlanta Hawks 2026-27 record: 7-5 Previous ranking: 18 Next games: @ CHI (Nov. 13), @ MIL (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Kingston Flemings With the Hawks' offense struggling early in the season, coach Quin Snyder inserted the rookie Flemings into the starting lineup and moved veteran CJ McCollum to a reserve role. The Hawks went on to win three out of the four games with Flemings as starter while ranking fifth in offense. Something to pay attention to is whether Snyder trusts Flemings to close games. In the past four games, he ranks eighth in minutes per game in the fourth quarter. -- Bobby Marks 15. Dallas Mavericks 2026-27 record: 7-4 Previous ranking: 13 Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 12), @ CLE (Nov. 14), @ BOS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Zaccharie Risacher The Mavericks took a flier on Risacher when they acquired him in the three-way trade that sent Luguentz Dort to Atlanta, hoping they could develop the former No. 1 pick into a quality role player. The 6-9 Risacher has impressed with his defensive activity as a reserve, averaging 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. Coach Dusty May is comfortable giving Risacher the assignment of guarding elite scorers across multiple positions. His defense on Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Kevin Durant helped the Mavs pull off wins over the Thunder and Rockets. -- MacMahon 16. Cleveland Cavaliers 2026-27 record: 5-6 Previous ranking: 9 Next games: @ NYK (Nov. 11), @ MIA (Nov. 13), vs. DAL (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: G Meleek Thomas Headline acquisition Peyton Watson is still struggling to find his footing in Cleveland, but Thomas, picked 34th in the 2026 draft, has been a pleasant surprise for the Cavaliers. The rookie guard shone at summer league and has carried over that performance to games that count, averaging 13 points and hitting 48% of his 3s so far. After starting the season with three DNPs in Cleveland's first five games, Thomas has quickly worked his way into playing 20-plus minutes every night. -- Zach Kram 17. Toronto Raptors 2026-27 record: 5-5 Previous ranking: 14 Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 11), @ PHI (Nov. 12), vs. NYK (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: F Allen Graves This should be going to Kawhi Leonard , who returned to Toronto in an offseason trade, but he has played only two games this season while sidelined with soreness in his left knee. The reality for the Raptors is that no newcomer has made a significant impact this season, but Graves, the team's first-round pick, has been the best of the team's additions, which include veteran Kyle Anderson and rookie Jaden Bradley . He has reached double digits once this season, scoring 11 points in a loss to Minnesota, and has largely played a depth role. -- Rhim 18. Miami Heat 2026-27 record: 5-6 Previous ranking: 19 Next games: vs. CLE (Nov. 13), vs. DET (Nov. 14), vs. HOU (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Giannis Antetokounmpo Even with the Heat's early-season struggles, it would be almost malpractice if we left Antetokounmpo off the list. After playing a career-low 36 games last season with Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo has appeared in all 10 games this season. The former MVP has scored 25 points or more in seven games and is on pace to average the most rebounds in his career since 2019-20. He is currently averaging a career-high 3.7 offensive rebounds. -- Marks 19. Washington Wizards 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 16 Next games: @ IND (Nov. 11), vs. DET (Nov. 12), vs. HOU (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Anthony Davis The 10-time All-Star counts as a newcomer, right? He technically joined the Wizards last February but didn't play a game for them until this season. All he has done with his new team is average 25.7 points and 9.7 rebounds this season. Washington is 4-5 when Davis plays and 0-2 when he doesn't, including a 39-point shellacking in Oklahoma City without the star big man on the court. -- Kram 20. New Orleans Pelicans 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 22 Next games: vs. BKN (Nov. 11), vs. MEM (Nov. 13), vs. DEN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Trendon Watford Coach Jamahl Mosley has largely relied on familiar faces while juggling his rotation due to injuries. Believe it or not, New Orleans' top eight scorers are all returning members of last year's 26-win team. Watford, a journeyman forward who joined the Pelicans on a minimum contract this summer, has worked his way into Mosley's rotation by averaging 7.2 points and 3.5 rebounds off the bench over the past six games. Meanwhile, Bennedict Mathurin , a 2022 lottery pick who inked a two-year, $15.4 million deal with New Orleans in free agency, is averaging a career-low 15.0 minutes per game. -- Golliver 21. Phoenix Suns 2026-27 record: 4-6 Previous ranking: 24 Next games: vs. CHA (Nov. 12), vs. LAL (Nov. 15), @ DEN (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: C Miles Bridges This year's Suns team, which ranks last in the league in rebounds per game, would be in even worse shape on the boards if not for Bridges securing a career-best 7.8 caroms per game -- two more than he averaged for the Charlotte Hornets last season. The 6-7 forward is also putting up 15.8 points, 3.2 assists and a career-high 1.2 steals per game. After starting the season 1-5, Phoenix won two out of its past three games, with Bridges averaging 9.3 rebounds during that stretch. -- McMenamin 22. Indiana Pacers 2026-27 record: 3-8 Previous ranking: 23 Next games: vs. WAS (Nov. 11), vs. NYK (Nov. 13), @ PHI (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: C Ivica Zubac Injuries have interrupted Zubac's total impact in his new home, but he played one of his best games of the season against the Mavericks this week, despite a modest box score -- 16 points on 5-of-7 shooting, but the team was a plus-6 while he was in the game. In spurts, he has shown there is room for more, especially as the Pacers get accustomed to his game while they await Tyrese Haliburton 's return to the lineup. -- Jamal Collier 23. Charlotte Hornets 2026-27 record: 4-7 Previous ranking: 20 Next games: @ PHX (Nov. 12), @ LAC (Nov. 15), @ LAL (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: G Grayson Allen Allen is averaging 15.3 points for the Hornets while making 47% of his 3-point tries. Charlotte ranks 28th in 3-point percentage as a team, but that's not Allen's fault. He ranks second in individual 3-point percentage (sandwiched between Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry ) out of 77 players with at least 50 attempts. -- Kram 24. Orlando Magic 2026-27 record: 3-7 Previous ranking: 21 Next games: @ UTAH (Nov. 11), vs. MIL (Nov. 13), @ BOS (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: G Tristan Da Silva Da Silva is not considered a newcomer since he was drafted in the 2024 first round. But with the injury to Paolo Banchero , Da Silva is averaging career highs in minutes (30.5) and points (15.1). He is also shooting 40% from 3. Da Silva was a new face to the Magic's starting five on Saturday night as he made his first start of the season in a loss to Golden State. -- Marks 25. LA Clippers 2026-27 record: 2-8 Previous ranking: 25 Next games: vs. OKC (Nov. 13), vs. CHA (Nov. 15), vs. UTAH (Nov. 17) Top newcomer: G Keaton Wagler The 6-5 guard, selected with the No. 5 pick out of Illinois, ranks fifth in 3-point percentage (39.0%) among rookies with at least 30 attempts. He has also found a way to generate points at the line, ranking second in total free throw attempts and second in free throw percentage (86.5%) among rookies with at least 30 trips to the line. As the Clippers begin their rebuild after the lackluster Kawhi Leonard - Paul George era, Wagler's development should be priority No. 1 for the franchise this season. -- McMenamin 26. Brooklyn Nets 2026-27 record: 2-8 Previous ranking: 29 Next games: @ NO (Nov. 11), @ MEM (Nov. 14), vs. PHI (Nov. 16) Top newcomer: F Julius Randle It has been hit or miss for Randle so far this season -- he has had bouts of being the most consistent Net on a team full of developing guards. He has had to create his own offense, which he might prefer, as Mikel Brown Jr . and Egor Demin are also battling injuries. He and Michael Porter Jr . can only play together so much because their styles clash, and on some nights like Sunday against Dallas, he'll be a minus-33 in a 130-93 loss. He's a proud veteran in a tough situation -- not an ideal one -- and the Nets have to find ways to maximize him on this ill-fitting team. -- Goodwill 27. Utah Jazz 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 26 Next games: vs. ORL (Nov. 11), @ HOU (Nov. 13), vs. SAS (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Darryn Peterson After a slow start, Darryn Peterson has started to get cooking, displaying the scoring ability that enticed the Jazz to draft him with the No. 2 pick. He has had his first three 20-point performances in the Jazz's past three games. Peterson has averaged 24 points on 51.9% shooting from the floor (11-of-24 on 3s) over those three games. -- MacMahon 28. Chicago Bulls 2026-27 record: 1-8 Previous ranking: 27 Next games: @ SAS (Nov. 11), vs. ATL (Nov. 13), @ MIN (Nov. 14) Top newcomer: F Caleb Wilson There haven't been many bright spots for the Bulls so far, but Wilson looks like he belongs. The early returns are strong at 19 points and six rebounds per game, yet his potential is tantalizing. He attacks the basket with intent to dunk everything, and his highlights on defense are eye-popping. Wilson isn't used to losing frequently, so with the Bulls in position to keep racking up L's, Chicago is already trying to manage his body language and effort. Tiago Splitter benched him last week against the Knicks because he noticed him getting down after missing some shots. Still, despite the growing pains, Wilson is easily the team's best newcomer. -- Collier 29. Milwaukee Bucks 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 28 Next games: vs. LAL (Nov. 11), @ ORL (Nov. 13), vs. ATL (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Brayden Burries Burries has already replaced Ryan Rollins in the Bucks' starting lineup, and he has easily been the biggest bright spot during a miserable start to the year in Milwaukee. He had the best game of his young career against the Raptors last week with 21 points, 11 rebounds and six assists. He has come out the gates as a great rebounder, and since moving to the starting lineup, he's averaging 13.0 points, 8.0 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 29 minutes. As the Bucks' season continues to slip away, Burries should get even more opportunities. -- Collier 30. Sacramento Kings 2026-27 record: 1-10 Previous ranking: 30 Next games: vs. POR (Nov. 13), vs. OKC (Nov. 15) Top newcomer: G Darius Acuff Jr. The No. 7 pick has opened his career with 20 or more shot attempts in 10 consecutive games, the longest streak for a rookie since Wilt Chamberlain (19 games) back in 1959. It hasn't all been cloaked in inefficiency, either. Acuff has made 45% or more of those shots in five of the past six games, showing greater comfort and passing willingness. He has games of 10, 12 and 14 assists during that stretch. Acuff recently: "Early on, I wasn't making as many reads. I was forcing a lot of shots. I think the game has slowed down for me." -- Slater

stories.summary: Brewer missed Wednesday’s practice for Miami.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins center Aaron Brewer (55) looks on after the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The injury woes keep piling up for the Miami Dolphins. This week, the Dolphins learned that starting defensive tackle Zach Sieler will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn biceps he suffered on the first play of Miami’s defeat against the Detroit Lions last Sunday. Starting quarterback Malik Willis was also placed on injured reserve due to a lingering groin injury — meaning Miami’s signal-caller will miss at least four games, if not more. If that wasn’t enough bad news for one week, on Wednesday, it was revealed that starting center Aaron Brewer is dealing with a concussion he suffered against Detroit and is currently in the league’s 5-step concussion protocol. As such, he missed Wednesday’s practice. This isn’t the first time this season that an offensive lineman for the Dolphins finished a game with no talk of a head injury, but exhibited symptoms in the subsequent days. Rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor missed Miami’s Week 8 tilt against the New England Patriots with the same issue. All eyes will now be on Miami’s practice reports throughout the rest of the week in order to see if Brewer will be able to clear protocol in time for the Dolphins’ Week 10 contest on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.
